subject: Postmortem readout & verification plan — tokenization stall (2028-02-27)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@covenantbank.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Postmortem readout & verification plan — tokenization stall (2028-02-27)

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our internal investigation. Attached is a short customer-facing RCA and a proposed verification plan. Below is a high-level summary and the concrete next steps we recommend.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Impact: tokenization stalls affected ~0.6% of requests for CovenantBank production pool between 02:03–02:26 UTC on 2028-02-27, causing API request timeouts and failed inference sessions.
- Root cause: a kernel-scheduling regression in our recent runtime release caused quantized-model routing to accept sessions while the KV-cache population for long-session affinity was incomplete, creating repeated KV-cache evictions and a tokenization stall loop.

Condensed timeline (full CSV attached):
- 02:02 UTC — rolling deploy of runtime v1.14.3 began targeting mixed-capacity pools.
- 02:05 UTC — low-level scheduler change started routing a subset of long-lived sessions to quantized variants.
- 02:07–02:26 UTC — repeated KV-cache misses + eviction cycle started for affected sessions; client retries compounded load and increased stalled session rate.
- 02:27 UTC — autoscale and fallback policies engaged; by 02:34 UTC traffic back to normal.

Immediate remediation already completed
1) Rolled back scheduler change in v1.14.3 at 02:30 UTC. (Owner: Dylan Brooks)
2) Temporary routing rule to pin sessions with affinity >30s to non-quantized variant. (Owner: David Kim)
3) Emergency autoscale parameters tightened for the affected Dedicated pool. (Owner: Hannah Schmitt)

Requested verification & next steps
A) Review and accept the attached customer RCA PDF (covenantbank-rca-summary-20280301.pdf).
B) Join a verification call so we can walk through the timeline and validate mitigations (I proposed Thu Mar 3, 15:00 ET — Calendly link below).
C) After your acceptance we will:
   - Ship a targeted patch (fix-4312.patch) to the dedicated pool and run the verification checklist. (Owner: Dylan — ETA: 2028-03-02 EOD)
   - Share post-deploy telemetry for your account and run the reproducibility tests you requested. (Owner: David — ETA: 2028-03-03)

Attachments: covenantbank-rca-summary-20280301.pdf, incident-timeline-20280227.csv
Links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/covenantbank-rca-20280301

I know reliability is paramount for CovenantBank — our team owned this incident end-to-end and we want to restore confidence quickly. Please let me know if the proposed times work or if you prefer a different cadence for verification.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@covenantbank.com>

Date: 2028-03-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Postmortem readout & verification plan — tokenization stall (2028-02-27)

Hi Stephanie,

Thank you for the quick turnaround and the clear summary. A couple of quick questions before we sign off on the plan:
- Can you provide the exact repro steps you used for the stuck sessions and a small anonymized log sample?
- Will the patch (fix-4312.patch) require a restart of our dedicated pool or will it be a hot fix?
- We want to make sure our internal SREs can run the verification checklist alongside your team — do you have a test harness or short instructions we can run pre-call?

We can do Thu Mar 3 at 15:00 ET — Elena + platform-ops will join.

Also, please include any proposed customer goodwill (service credit) language in the call — our procurement team will ask.

Regards,
Elena Morris
Head of Platform Operations, CovenantBank
elena.morris@covenantbank.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@covenantbank.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Postmortem readout & verification plan — tokenization stall (2028-02-27)

Elena — thanks, noted. Quick answers inline and a link to a pre-call test harness.

- Repro steps & logs: see section 2 of the attached PDF for sanitized repro steps. We’ll also paste a 50-line anonymized sample on the verification link before the call.
- Patch impact: fix-4312.patch is a hot-path scheduler guard; it can be rolled out without full pool restarts if run as a staged canary (we will coordinate the canary windows with you).
- Test harness: short instructions and the harness are in the verification-checklist.xlsx and the shared Drive folder. The harness is a lightweight runner that will hit your Dedicated pool with session-affinity patterns and report KV-hit/miss stats.

Proposed customer goodwill: we can include a 10% invoice credit for the affected billing period, subject to your procurement approval. We’ll have formal language ready at the call.

Call: Thu Mar 3, 15:00 ET — calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/rca-verification-20280303

I’m attaching the verification checklist and will post the anonymized log excerpt to the Drive later today.

Attachments: verification-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Stephanie
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@covenantbank.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Postmortem readout & verification plan — tokenization stall (2028-02-27)

Hi Elena / Stephanie — short technical confirmation ahead of tomorrow's call.

Status update:
- fix-4312.patch has been deployed to a canary subset of the Dedicated pool at 13:20 PT and promoted account-by-account following initial health checks.
- Observed metrics from canary: stalled-session rate dropped from ~0.6% to <0.02% within 12 minutes; KV-hit ratio increased ~9 percentage points for long-affinity sessions.

Hot-fix and verification notes (for your SREs):
1) Hot-path guard toggles a scheduler flag (scheduler.force_nonquantize_on_affinity) — no restart required when toggled in Canary; full pool promotion is a rolling reconfigure that does not require instance restarts.
2) Repro steps (sanitized): run harness with session length distribution skewed to >30s, 2–4 concurrent global clients, and intermittent tokenization token delays. The harness will emit KV-hit/miss stats to the shared folder.
3) Sample log snippet (sanitized):
   [2028-02-27T02:10:07Z] pool=dedicated-covenantbank session_id=abc123 kv_miss=true eviction_count=3 stall_detected=true
   [2028-02-27T02:11:03Z] pool=dedicated-covenantbank session_id=abc123 kv_hit=false eviction_count=4 stall_detected=true

We will upload a larger sanitized sample to the Drive and the verification-run results after the scheduled canary promotion. Please let me know if you want us to delay full promotion until you run your in-house harness — we can pause.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
